title: Thermodynamics of the space of trajectories governed by a combination of two additive boundary functionals
abstract: This paper extends the formalism of stochastic path-space thermodynamics by systematically expanding the space of thermodynamic variables with a spectrum of boundary and relative functionals of random processes. Generalizing the approaches introduced in preprints arXiv:2607.24078 and arXiv:2609.08477, we investigate the fluctuation statistics of a one-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with an asymmetric linear drift and a step penalty potential at the origin, which models the waiting phase of a molecular Brownian motor. Utilizing the Feynman-Kac formalism and the parabolic cylinder theory, a numerical scheme based on matching logarithmic derivatives via the secant method is constructed. A high-precision eigenvalues of the effective Hamiltonian is obtained, which define the cumulant generating function. We formulate a modified path-space fluctuation theorem of the Gallavotti-Cohen type for the conjugate drift current at a fixed integral occupation time of the system in the dissipative half-plane. The physical and thermodynamic significance of the new variables is elucidated. A combination of "residence time" and "integral current" functionals is applied to describe an ion channel sensitive to mechanical or electrical stimuli.
summary: This work advances stochastic path-space thermodynamics by expanding the set of measurable thermodynamic variables to include complex boundary functionals like residence time and integral current. Using the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process as a model, the authors derive generalized fluctuation theorems and analyze how external forces break Onsager symmetry in the system's free-energy landscape. This provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous framework for understanding non-equilibrium processes in molecular motors and ion channels.
main_problem: The paper extends stochastic path-space thermodynamics by systematically incorporating a broad spectrum of boundary and relative functionals of random processes into the description of thermodynamic variables.
main_result: It derives a modified path-space fluctuation theorem of the Gallavotti-Cohen type and establishes an exact thermodynamic potential for systems governed by combinations of two additive functionals.
method: The analysis employs the Feynman-Kac formalism and parabolic cylinder theory to calculate the joint Laplace transform, leading to the determination of the effective Hamiltonian's eigenvalues.
model_or_system: The primary model is a one-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, used to simulate the waiting phase of a molecular Brownian motor or an ion channel sensitive to external stimuli.
key_observables: Residence time ($	au_+$), integral current ($	ext{T}_I$), Maximal Deficit (Maximum Drawdown), and the mutual cross-sensitivity coefficient ($\chi_{12}$).
important_parameters: The analysis explores regimes far from equilibrium, such as the deep suppression regime ($	au^+ 	o 0$) and the continuous activation regime ($	au^+ 	o 1$), and the effect of external drift ($V$).
main_assumptions: The framework relies on the mathematical tractability afforded by considering the combination of only two additive functionals, and the system dynamics are modeled by the OU process.
figures_summary: The figures illustrate the topographic contour map of the path-space free energy profile, showing the transition from symmetric quadratic ellipses near equilibrium to asymmetric, non-parabolic contours when far from equilibrium or when external drifts break symmetry.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds its argument by first extending the formalism via boundary functionals, then detailing the mathematical framework using the Feynman-Kac approach for the OU process, applying it to a biological ion channel model, and finally discussing the derived results and implications.
why_interesting: While focused on classical stochastic processes, the rigorous application of fluctuation theorems and the extension of thermodynamic variables into path space provide powerful mathematical tools applicable to open quantum systems where non-equilibrium dynamics are crucial.
